projects.title: Municipal Data Migration and Reconciliation Pipeline
projects.status: Delivered per Pourashava; reused across administrations
projects.problem: Holding-tax and trade-license registers from several Pourashavas, arrived as Excel, PDF or Word with corrupted Bengali text and inconsistent columns, and had to land in a multi-table production schema.
projects.solution: Staging tables, a rule engine encoding the SOP, composite Bengali cell extraction, foreign-key ID resolution, a transactional INSERT...SELECT with a generated account number, and reversible correction scripts.
tricky: SILENT CORRUPTION: the ACE OLEDB driver guessed column types in staging, so mixed text/number columns lost Bengali text with no error. Fix: explicit typing plus a source-vs-loaded cell-count check.
INVISIBLE MISMATCH: precomposed and decomposed Bengali characters (nukta forms) look identical but never match. Fix: NFC-normalize both sides before any compare.
SAFE FIXES: corrections written as transactional, reversible scripts on a stable join key, so any change can be traced and undone.
RULE-BASED IDs: account numbers built from a zero-padded prefix, a constant, and a running number with a length rule; one off-by-one breaks every record after it.
resume: Municipal Data Migration and Reconciliation Pipeline

Co-developed (AI-assisted) source-to-target mapping, staging and record-level validation scripts for municipal trade-license, holding-tax and payment-history data across multi-table SQL Server schemas; added explicit typing, Unicode normalisation and source-versus-loaded count checks after finding silent text loss caused by driver type-guessing.

projects.title: Tax-Head, Arrear & Bill Engine
projects.problem: The master table stores one total tax amount per holding, but the child tables need one line per tax head (holding, water, lighting, conservancy and others), plus arrear and bill rows, and every administration has different head IDs and rates.
projects.solution: Separate scripts were merged into one configuration-driven Streamlit app whose modules are discovered from a JSON list, so a new module needs no edits to existing code. Each administration's head catalog (IDs and rates) is loaded from configuration. For each holding, rows are generated only for the heads that apply, arrear and surcharge are split by each head's rate share, and the arrear-opening and bill files are produced with pre-load validation.
tricky: ROW MAPPING: one holding row in the master file becomes one child row per applicable head only. A head with no rate is skipped, not written as a zero row.
PROPORTIONAL SPLIT: a 10% total made of 7% holding and 3% water splits arrear 7/10 and 3/10, not evenly across heads.

EQUAL AMOUNTS, DIFFERENT RATES: two heads can show the same amount (for example 113.01 each) while their real rates are 7 and 3, so split weights come from the fixed catalog rate per head, never from the amount columns.
EXACT TOTALS: the split parts add back to the original amount to the paisa, using largest-remainder rounding.
TWO INPUT SHAPES: some files carry a total tax rate that is matched against the catalog; others carry a rate column per head, where any value above zero means that head applies. Both are supported.
AMBIGUOUS RATE MATCHING: a 10% total can be built from several head combinations, so the engine combines ordered (prefix) matching with combinatorial rate matching.
NO SHARED IDS: two administrations had completely non-overlapping head IDs, so nothing is hard-coded; the catalog is configuration.
FREE-HOST LIMITS: files of about 150,000 rows were slow and crashed on a free host; the head-matching engine was vectorized.
resume: Co-developed (AI-assisted) a configuration-driven tool, merged from separate scripts, that loads each administration's tax-head catalog and rates, generates one child row per applicable head, splits arrear and surcharge by each head's rate share with exact-total rounding, and prepares arrear-opening and bill data with pre-load validation.

projects.title: Trade License Reconciliation & Entry Automation
projects.status: Reconciliation delivered; portal automation in progress (needs BASE_URL and a full Codegen recording)
projects.problem: Trade-license registers from more than one Pourashava had duplicate license numbers, missing fees and Bengali spelling variants.
projects.solution: Three-stage pipeline (convert, scrape, UI entry) with row-level status, JSONL audit logs and a 36-column entry-ready schema. Reconciliation matched on mobile number plus business name, which found 15 genuinely missing records in one 450-row register. Fee and street normalization follow strict rules (fees never decrease).
tricky: BAD KEY: license number had duplicates, so it cannot identify a row. Matching on mobile number plus business name found 15 genuinely missing records in one 450-row register.
NEVER-DECREASE RULE: when merging near-identical fees, the fee may only go up, and fee, VAT and total must all update together.
RESUMABLE RUNS: row-level status plus JSONL audit log, and a resume key that is the row serial, not the license number.
CONFIG TRAP: module-level environment reads ignore .env overrides; config must load lazily. A date constant was defined but never wired to the page call.
SILENT DATE BUG: precomposed versus decomposed Bengali characters in one column header made a lookup fail and assigned the wrong date to every row; fixed by NFC-normalising headers before matching.

THREE-BUCKET PRE-VALIDATION: before any batch run each row is classed Ready, Needs review or Excluded, with audit columns written back to Excel; ambiguous rows were held back for manual review instead of being submitted.

projects.title: Bijoy/SutonnyMJ to Unicode Conversion Utility
projects.problem: Legacy ANSI Bengali (SutonnyMJ/Bijoy) is unreadable by modern tools.
projects.solution: Installable Python package with a Streamlit app (single-file and bulk tabs) covering DOCX, XLSX, XLS, CSV and PDF, a patched glyph map and fixes for reph ordering and pre-base vowels. Modules can be switched on or off from a JSON file, and a pytest suite guards it. Also run as customized scripts that convert Bengali text across whole database tables.
tricky: REPH ORDER: the reph must move after the consonant cluster; pre-base vowels must move before it.
HAND-TYPED TRAP: Bengali text typed into regexes can be silently decomposed, so patterns never match; build them from code points.
PDF TABLES: dynamic schema detection and ward-column state tracking across page breaks.
OOXML ORDER: Word rejected converted DOCX files because the font element was appended last instead of in schema order; fixed with a schema-position helper and a regression test.
PDF SPACE LOSS: pdfplumber's character API drops spaces, so spacing is rebuilt explicitly.
INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION: outputs are re-read with a different library from the one that wrote them, and each delivery is tested from a fresh extraction.
resume: Co-developed (AI-assisted) an installable converter for legacy font-encoded Bengali text in DOCX, XLSX, XLS, CSV and PDF files, with a Streamlit interface and a pytest suite; named regression bugs (schema-order XML error, PDF space loss, numeric-cell coercion) were reproduced from real files before fixing. Also run as scripts over whole database text.

projects.title: Centralized Municipal Tax Platform: Phased Pourashava Onboarding
projects.problem: Every Pourashava has its own tax heads, rates, ward and street structures and legacy data formats, yet a centralized platform needs all of them to behave consistently as they are connected one phase at a time.
projects.solution: I map and load each Pourashava's data and verify it against its source. The approach is configuration-driven onboarding instead of per-site code, reconciled loads, and regression checks so that each new connection does not disturb those already live.

projects.title: Reusable Test Automation Framework
projects.status: Working; used on a trade-license batch-entry project (in progress)
projects.solution: Record, generate and run: page classes and locator files are generated and safe to regenerate, while hand-written subclasses and tests are scaffolded once and never overwritten. Real named Page Object methods replace a generic dispatcher, with pytest-html reports, session reuse and screenshots on pass or fail, and a folder per site so projects do not collide.
resume: Co-developed (AI-assisted) a Page Object Model framework with scaffold-once code generation and a pre-validation step that classes each data row as Ready, Needs review or Excluded before batch runs; applied to a trade-license batch-entry project (in progress).
